To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the conformational stabilities of β‐sheet proteins can be determined by measuring the high‐frequency amides I component of their ir spectra, and that the stability of the β‐sheet protein, RNase A, is ∼ 1.6 kcal/mol, and is comparable to the stability of a typical α‐helix protein.

1) a characteristic high‐ frequency amide I component is observed in the FTIR difference spectra of β‐sheets; 2) the high‐frequency amides I component is fairly narrow, ∼ 8– 10 cm−1, and can be quantitively resolved; 3) this high‐ frequency component can be used to determine the conformational stabilities of β‐sheet proteins.

(i) a new method for measuring β-sheet stability is developed, (ii) the new method is applicable to a wide range of systems, (iii) the new method provides results that are consistent with the literature, and (iv) the new method has been applied to the study of a novel β-hairpin peptide.
